references.text: The Lord says that the sin of Sodom and Gomorrah is so great that he will go down to see if what they have done fully matches the outcry that has come up to him.
The Lord rained sulfur and fire down on Sodom and Gomorrah from heaven, destroying these cities and the entire plain – this is the destruction whose result Abraham now sees.
Mount Sinai shook because the Lord descended upon it in fire, and smoke rose up "like the smoke of a furnace" – the same imagery as in Gen 19:28.
The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah with sulfur and fire is mentioned as a warning of God's judgment on apostate lands.
Sodom and Gomorrah were reduced to ashes and made an example for the ungodly in times to come.
Smoke rose from the abyss "like smoke from a great furnace" – a linguistic echo of the smoke from Sodom's destruction.
The kings of the earth see the smoke from Babylon's burning, which recalls Abraham looking down on the smoke from Sodom's destruction.
Jude confirms that the visible punishment in Genesis is an example of eternal judgment against sin.
